description: Competency questions defining the scope of the wound ontology. Organised by clinical question. Questions the ontology must answer (in_scope) or explicitly cannot answer (out_of_scope).

clinical_themes.theme: What is a wound? What is not a wound?

in_scope.question: Is a diabetic wound a type of wound?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'Diabetic Foot Ulcer is_a Chronic Wound'. No wound class is chronic by definition (every wound starts acute), so nothing may be asserted under Chronic wound; and WONT models the diabetic wound, not the foot site. The subsumption asked for is the one WONT holds.

in_scope.question: Is a pressure ulcer a type of wound?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'is_a Chronic Wound' -- same reason as CQ001. Expected to FAIL until WONT mints its own pressure ulcer class (the label currently resolves to HP_0012399, a phenotype); see WONT_TODO.

in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'Venous Leg Ulcer is_a Chronic Wound' -- same reason as CQ001. The venous axis is what WONT asserts of this class (label 'Wound co-located with impaired venous backflow' until 2026-09-17).

out_of_scope.question: Is a bone fracture a wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Fracture is an orthopaedic injury — not a soft-tissue wound concept in this ontology.

out_of_scope.question: Is a myocardial infarction a wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Organ infarction is not within the wound care domain.

in_scope.question: What causes a pressure injury?
in_scope.rewrite: 'caused_by' -> 'co_located_with' (2026-09) -> 'complication_of' (2026-09-17). MILD commitment 4 refuses aetiology between disorders; the assertable question is whether the subject is the output of a development process that has a wound causing process of the object's disease course as part (MILD_120053). Co-location only said a diagnostic classification files the two under one disease.

in_scope.note: REVERTED a label fix. Mapping 'Wound Complication' to 'wound complication process' made this triple a category error: Wound dehiscence is a MILD_120022 pathological disorder, not a process, so it can never be a subclass of a process. The ontology's material counterpart is 'material complication disease entity' - but choosing it is a modelling decision, not a label fix, so it is left for review.

in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'has_quality Malignant'. WONT defines Malignant wound through its causal history (output of a wound development process that has a wound causing malignant process as part), not through a quality of the wound; malignancy is a disposition of a tumour. The question now asks what the ontology asserts.
